subsystems.name: Sample acquisition and preparation
subsystems.role: gets a solid sample into the instrument without contaminating it or losing the gases it holds.

subsystems.name: Evolved-gas furnace
subsystems.role: heats the sample in a sealed oven so volatiles and combustion products come off for analysis.

subsystems.name: Mass-analyser core
subsystems.role: separates ionised gas molecules by mass-to-charge ratio.

subsystems.name: Isobaric-resolution stage
subsystems.role: resolves molecules of nearly identical mass, for example ¹³CH₄ from ¹²CH₃D, which a low-resolution analyser cannot separate.

subsystems.name: Micro-scale ion probe
subsystems.role: maps isotope ratios within a single mineral grain instead of averaging a bulk sample.
parts: focused primary ion or laser beam

subsystems.name: Calibration and standards system
subsystems.role: every ratio is meaningless without comparison to a known reference, so reference gases are measured alongside the sample.

subsystems.name: Blank and contamination control
subsystems.role: the instrument must prove the signal came from the sample, not from the plumbing or the surrounding air.

buildSteps.title: Fix the scientific target
buildSteps.detail: Decide which isotope systems matter — carbon-13 depletion for organic matter, sulfur-34 fractionation for microbial sulfate reduction — and what precision is needed to tell biology from abiotic chemistry.

buildSteps.title: Design the gas path
buildSteps.detail: Lay out a leak-tight manifold of valves and ovens so a sample can be heated, its gases swept, and reference gases admitted under identical conditions.

buildSteps.title: Build the ion source and analyser
buildSteps.detail: Assemble an electron-impact source and a mass analyser with enough resolving power to separate interfering isobars; this sets the instrument's accuracy ceiling.

buildSteps.title: Add a vacuum system
buildSteps.detail: Pumps and seals must reach high vacuum, or in a thin planetary atmosphere must pump down from ambient pressure; bake-out keeps residual water and carbon dioxide from swamping the peaks.

buildSteps.title: Wire in the calibration standards
buildSteps.detail: Known reference gases and mineral standards are plumbed in so the instrument can bracket every measurement and correct for its own fractionation.

buildSteps.title: Characterise performance
buildSteps.detail: Run blanks, standards and synthetic mixtures to establish accuracy, precision and detection limits before trusting any real sample.

buildSteps.title: Put it through a flight or field qualification
buildSteps.detail: Vibration, thermal-vacuum and radiation testing, or field trials, prove the instrument survives its journey and keeps its calibration.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and interpret
buildSteps.detail: Measure the sample, correct the raw ratios, and then interpret the numbers against abiotic processes such as thermal cracking or serpentinisation that can mimic part of the biological signal.

prerequisites.why: the measurement basis: gas-source magnetic-sector instruments set the accuracy benchmark on Earth.
they give micrometre-scale maps so a ratio can be tied to a specific grain rather than a bulk average.

prerequisites.tech: Sample acquisition on a planetary surface
prerequisites.why: rock must be drilled, powdered and delivered to a sealed oven without introducing terrestrial carbon or sulfur.

prerequisites.tech: Isotopic reference materials for Mars-like minerals
prerequisites.why: calibration needs standards matched to sulfates, carbonates and perchlorates; coverage for these matrices is still thin.
without knowing how much fractionation non-biological chemistry produces, a biosignature cannot be claimed with confidence.

pathway.milestone: routine Earth-laboratory isotope analysis and micrometre-scale ion-probe mapping of ancient sediments
pathway.unlocks: isotopic evidence for early life on Earth that survives the loss of molecular fossils.

pathway.milestone: in-situ evolved-gas and isotope measurements on Mars, as with the Sample Analysis at Mars instrument on the Curiosity rover
pathway.unlocks: first-order carbon and sulfur isotope data from another planet, though with coarser precision than a terrestrial lab.

pathway.milestone: returned Mars samples analysed in Earth laboratories
pathway.unlocks: the precision and reference-standard control that no flight instrument can currently match.

pathway.milestone: instruments flown to icy-moon plumes and ocean worlds
pathway.unlocks: isotope testing of subsurface oceans where liquid water may persist for long periods.

pathway.milestone: miniaturised, standards-integrated isotope labs on landers
pathway.unlocks: life-detection claims that do not depend on returning a sample to Earth.
